walkthroughs.body_html:
A business can be profitable on paper but still go bust.

That happens if customers pay LATE while suppliers and staff need paying NOW.
A cash-flow forecast lists inflows (sales, loans, investment), outflows (raw materials, wages, rent, utilities), and the closing balance for each month.

Bank managers want to see one before lending.

If a forecast shows months of negative cash, owners can plan: arrange an overdraft, delay spending, push for faster payments.

mcqs.q: Which is a cash OUTFLOW for a typical retailer?
options: Customer sales
Wages paid
Owner's investment
Bank loan received
Inflows minus outflows
Inflows plus outflows
Sales minus costs of sales
Sales minus all costs

mcqs.q: Why can a profitable business still fail?
options: Because cash flow and profit are different — a business may be profitable on paper but run out of cash to pay bills, especially if customers owe money or stock ties up funds.
Profitable businesses fail only when employees steal.
Cash flow only matters at year-end.
If a business is profitable it cannot run out of money.

mcqs.q: Why are cash flow and profit different on different time-scales?
options: Profit is recognised when a sale is made (even on credit); cash flow is when money actually moves. A profitable sale today may produce no cash for 60 days while bills are due — creating a cash-flow problem despite profit.
Cash flow only matters at year-end.
Cash flow and profit are the same thing measured differently.
Profitable businesses fail only when employees steal.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between gross profit and net profit?
options: Gross profit is profit before VAT and net profit is profit after VAT.
Gross profit = revenue minus cost of goods sold (direct costs only); net profit = revenue minus ALL costs including overheads, interest and tax. Net profit is the bottom line.
Gross profit and net profit are the same thing.
Cash flow only matters at year-end.
